Check a Penalty Numerically

Source: R/check_penalty.R
check_penalty.Rd

Compares the derivatives that a penalty declares with numerical references, and returns one row per comparison carrying the worst scaled error and a pass or fail. The gradient is compared with a numDeriv gradient of the value, and the Hessian with a numerical Jacobian of the analytic gradient. Each hyperparameter gradient is compared with a numerical derivative of the value in that hyperparameter, each entry of the hyperparameter Hessian, diagonal or off-diagonal, with a numerical derivative of the analytic hyperparameter gradient, and each mixed block with a numerical Jacobian of the analytic coefficient gradient, so that a reference is never a difference of another difference. For a quadratic penalty, the function also tests the three-point identity, the log pseudo-determinant, the rank and the null basis. The function serves to verify the derivatives of a penalty written by the user.

Usage

check_penalty(pen, beta = NULL, theta = NULL, tol = 1e-06, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

pen

A penalty() object, of any branch.

beta

A numeric coefficient vector of length pen@n_coef. NULL, the default, draws one from rnorm(sd = 1.3) rounded to two places and shifted by 0.11, then moves it away from the kinks as above. The draw is taken from a fixed seed, so the report is the same on two runs, and the caller's own .Random.seed is restored on exit (or removed, if there was none), so a call in the middle of a simulation leaves that simulation unchanged.

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values, or a named numeric vector carrying the same. NULL, the default, places each hyperparameter six tenths of the way across its own bounds, reading an infinite lower bound as -1 and an infinite upper bound as two above the lower. That gives lambda = 1.2 for a hyperparameter bounded on \((0, \infty)\), alpha = 0.6 for the elastic net, a = 3.2 for SCAD and gamma = 2.2 for MCP.

tol

The scaled error at or above which a row is reported as FAILED. It is a single positive number, 1e-6 by default. A row whose error is not finite is also reported as FAILED, and so is a row whose numerical reference cannot be computed.

verbose

TRUE, the default, prints the table without row names. The result is returned invisibly either way.

Value

A data frame with one row per check and three columns: check (character, the row's name as tabulated above), max_error (numeric) and status (character, "OK" or "FAILED"). The data frame is returned invisibly. For the rows that compare with a numerical reference, max_error is the worst absolute difference divided by max(1, max(abs(reference))). For the three-point identity it is the absolute value of the combination divided by max(1, abs(rho(beta))); for the slope of the log pseudo-determinant, the absolute difference between the increase and the rank; for the rank and for the width of the null basis, the absolute difference between the two counts; for the annihilation by the null basis, the largest absolute entry of \(S(\theta)N\) divided by max(1, max(abs(S))). A row whose reference signals an error, a numerical derivative or the eigenvalues of the rank row, has max_error equal to NaN.

The rows

Two rows are produced for every penalty, three more for each hyperparameter, one more for each pair of distinct hyperparameters, and four or five more when is_quadratic() is TRUE:

rowcompares
gradient vs numDerivpenalty_gradient() against a numerical gradient of penalty_value()
hessian vs numDeriv on the gradientpenalty_hessian() against a numerical Jacobian of the analytic gradient, symmetrized
grad_theta[p] vs numDerivpenalty_grad_theta() against a numerical derivative of the value in hyperparameter p
hess_theta[p_p] vs numDerivthe diagonal entry of penalty_hess_theta() against a numerical derivative of the analytic grad_theta
hess_theta[p_r] vs numDerivthe off-diagonal entry of penalty_hess_theta() for hyperparameters p and r, with p before r in pen@params, against a numerical derivative in r of the analytic grad_theta of p
cross[p] vs Richardson on the gradientpenalty_cross() against a numerical Jacobian of the analytic coefficient gradient in p
quadratic three-point identity\(\rho(2\beta) - 4\rho(\beta) + 3\rho(0)\), which vanishes when the value is a quadratic form with no linear term
logpdet linear in log lambda with slope rraising lambda by a factor of \(e\) raises the value of penalty_logpdet() by the rank
logpdet gradient vs numDerivthe grad element of penalty_logpdet() against a numerical derivative of its value
rank vs eigenvalues of the matrixpenalty_rank() against the number of eigenvalues of \(S(\theta)\), or of the sum of the normalized components of an additive penalty, that exceed a relative tolerance times the largest
null basis width vs n_coef minus rankthe number of columns of penalty_null_basis() against pen@n_coef minus penalty_rank()
null basis annihilates the matrix\(S(\theta)N\), where \(S(\theta)\) is penalty_matrix() and \(N\) is penalty_null_basis()

The two log pseudo-determinant rows are alternatives, as described below. The row of the annihilation appears only when the null basis has columns. With \(p\) hyperparameters the count is therefore \(2 + 3p + p(p-1)/2\) for a penalty that is not quadratic, and four or five more for a quadratic one. A lasso gives 5 rows, SCAD 9, a full-rank ridge 9, a quadratic penalty over second differences 10, and a structured penalty over a 3 x 3 log-Cholesky precision 39.

Which log pseudo-determinant row a quadratic branch gets

The quadratic rows are produced for every branch for which is_quadratic() returns TRUE: the three-point identity, one of the two log pseudo-determinant rows, the row of the rank, the row of the width of the null basis, and the row of the annihilation when the null basis has columns. When "lambda" is among pen@params, the matrix is one scale times a constant, the log pseudo-determinant is linear in \(\log\lambda\) with slope the rank, and the row tests that identity. Otherwise the matrix depends on several hyperparameters, as in a structured or an additive penalty, and the row compares the reported gradient with a numerical derivative of the value. A two-component additive penalty whose sum has a null space therefore produces 14 rows: the 9 rows of its two hyperparameters, the three-point identity, the gradient of the log pseudo-determinant, the rank, the width of the null basis and its annihilation. When the sum has full rank the row of the annihilation is absent and the count is 13.

The row of the rank counts the eigenvalues that exceed a relative tolerance times the largest. For a quadratic or a structured penalty they are the eigenvalues of \(S(\theta)\) at the theta of the check. For an additive penalty they are the eigenvalues of the sum of the components after each has been divided by its largest absolute entry, so that the row reproduces the count of additive_penalty(): a count on \(S(\theta)\) drops the smaller components once their scales differ by more than the tolerance, as that function's page describes. The tolerance is the tol stored in a quadratic or an additive penalty, the one given to its constructor, and 1e-10 for a structured penalty, which stores none. The row's max_error is the absolute difference between that count and penalty_rank(). A stored rank that differs from the count by one or more therefore fails the row of the rank, and a null basis whose number of columns differs from pen@n_coef minus the stored rank fails the row of the width.

What is not checked

The check covers the value and its derivatives on the parameter scale, and the quantities that a marginal criterion reads. It does not test the hess element of penalty_logpdet(), the scale = "link" option of the hyperparameter derivatives, is_proper(), penalty_prox(), penalty_prox_spec(), penalty_dhessian(), penalty_d2hessian(), penalty_dcross(), penalty_dhessian_beta(), penalty_d2hessian_beta(), penalty_dhessian_beta_theta(), penalty_draw() or penalty_readable(). It calls penalty_kinks() to place the coefficients but does not test the kinks themselves.

Where the coefficients are placed

A penalty with a kink has no derivative there, so a numerical reference that straddles one measures the kink and not the formula. If beta is NULL, 0.033 is added to every coefficient, up to fifty times, until every coordinate of \(D\beta\) lies more than 0.05 from every kink that penalty_kinks() returns. A draw that already clears the kinks is used unchanged, and after fifty steps the last draw is used whether or not it clears them.

Errors

numDeriv is in Suggests and the derivative rows need it, so the function signals an error when it is not installed. A theta outside the penalty's open bounds or missing a hyperparameter is rejected before any check runs. The analytic methods are evaluated at beta and theta outside the numerical references, so an error in penalty_value(), penalty_gradient(), penalty_hessian(), the hyperparameter derivatives or the quadratic quantities is signaled as it arises. An error inside a numerical reference is not signaled: numDeriv stops when the function that it differentiates returns a value that is not finite, and the row whose reference stopped is then reported with max_error equal to NaN and status FAILED, while the other rows are computed as usual.

See also

penalty_value() and penalty_gradient() for the quantities checked, penalty_kinks() for the set that the coefficients avoid, numericals7::check_abs_smoother() for the same check on a smoother, linkfunctions7::check_link() and distributions7::check_distrib() for the corresponding checks of a link and of a distribution.

Examples

# The penalty over first differences of five coefficients has rank 4 and one
# null direction.
pen <- quadratic_penalty(crossprod(diff(diag(5))))
res <- check_penalty(pen)
#>                                        check    max_error status
#>                         gradient vs numDeriv 4.007727e-11     OK
#>          hessian vs numDeriv on the gradient 7.928288e-12     OK
#>               grad_theta[lambda] vs numDeriv 1.851376e-11     OK
#>        hess_theta[lambda_lambda] vs numDeriv 1.488393e-11     OK
#>  cross[lambda] vs Richardson on the gradient 1.291110e-11     OK
#>               quadratic three-point identity 2.296653e-16     OK
#>    logpdet linear in log lambda with slope r 4.440892e-16     OK
#>            rank vs eigenvalues of the matrix 0.000000e+00     OK
#>        null basis width vs n_coef minus rank 0.000000e+00     OK
#>            null basis annihilates the matrix 2.775558e-16     OK
all(res$status == "OK")
#> [1] TRUE

# A separable penalty has fewer rows: no matrix, so no quadratic checks.
nrow(check_penalty(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 4), verbose = FALSE))
#> [1] 5

# A penalty with a wrong gradient fails the rows that read the gradient.
# The broken method is registered on a subclass, because registering it on
# the real class would change the generic for the rest of the session.
Broken <- S7::new_class("Broken", parent = QuadraticPenalty)
bad <- do.call(Broken, S7::props(quadratic_penalty(diag(3))))
S7::method(penalty_gradient, Broken) <- function(pen, beta, theta, ...) {
  1.05 * S7::method(penalty_gradient, QuadraticPenalty)(pen, beta, theta, ...)
}
failed <- check_penalty(bad, verbose = FALSE)
failed[failed$status != "OK", c("check", "max_error")]
#>                                         check  max_error
#> 1                        gradient vs numDeriv 0.05000000
#> 2         hessian vs numDeriv on the gradient 0.04761905
#> 5 cross[lambda] vs Richardson on the gradient 0.04761905
